answer: Require every agent identity to be anchored by a costly, verifiable credential — a hardware-attested key plus a refundable bond — before it can earn trust. Newcomers start with a sparrow's weight: no reputation, capped influence, and rate-limited actions, so creating thousands of fake identities costs real money and hardware, not just code. Reputation accrues only through checkable work, and misbehavior burns the bond and the identity. Honest agents keep a safe haven of trust, while an attacker facing an ocean of worthless fakes must pay again for every one they lose.
